reason: Recurring manual workflow this episode: harvesting Threads posts for bank/ewallet entities into staging manual_threads. Lessons captured: complaint-specific queries beat brand-only queries, promo posts must be filtered, Loading results are partial, the insert must be idempotent and timezone-correct, and aggregates are not refreshed by the insert. No existing skill covers manual source harvesting.

Episode showed missing category-sweep coverage rules and attribution/verification steps: user had to point out that only "bca"/"dana" queries missed the viral Flip case, and that the category must be finished entity by entity ("sampai tuntas"). A post was also filed under the wrong entity (Jago 375 got 0 rows, Bank Jago 364 got the posts), caught only by per-entity count verification.

Episode harvested 25+ public figures into manual_threads. A placeholder post code was typed, then patched in the ledger with sed. The skill has no ledger or no-opinion convention, so each run reinvents it and risks guessed codes.

Scraping 25 figures via browser_batch with page text plus a JS link extractor worked well and was not documented. The skill's only browser line is a generic one. Also, news and survey reposts appeared in results and needed filtering by hand.

Data minimization (docs/15, index rule: never store usernames). The skill forbids post text but is silent on usernames, and the scrape output is full of them. The episode kept usernames out of the ledger and insert by design; the skill should say so.

The episode's insert used `$now = now()` for observed_at because the scrape had no timestamps, which contradicts the skill's parse-timestamp rule with no fallback. The skill needs the fallback so the next run is not forced to choose silently.
Trigger wording missed the user's real phrasing (sentimen, komentar, tokoh/person); widen the routing sentence so the skill fires on the words a user actually types.

User explicitly wanted comments included, not only posts. The batch harvested top-level SERP posts only and the report admitted comments were almost absent. Make the gap and the permalink path explicit so the next run does not repeat it silently.

User repeatedly asked to continue in batches of 50 with no re-prompting. The batch picked its own ordering from the DB; make that choice stated and the per-batch report consistent so the user can steer.

The batch surfaced repeated false matches on common and historical names, and one vendor sitting in the person category. The skill's attribution section only covered brand/app overlap. Add the person-specific collision rule and the flag-don't-fix rule.

First ssh attempt with the default key was refused and the run stalled until the user granted access. The working invocation (explicit key, IdentitiesOnly, BatchMode) belongs in the skill so the next run does not rediscover it. Host and key path left out of the body because the repo is public.

The documented output line did not match what the insert script actually printed, so a reader cannot tell a clean run from a broken one. Align the expected output with the real format and add the row-count check.

The first verify run reported zero-count entities as positions 0,1,3,4… instead of entity ids. It was caught only because the numbers looked implausible. Make the id-mapping rule and the output-parsing rule explicit so the verify step cannot silently mislead.
Skill described the search URL only in prose. The exact working URL shape used in every batch goes in the body so the next run does not guess the query parameters.

The 100-character cut was used for a real entity (Jokowi) and the agent accepted it as "enough for flow, not for scoring"; the classifier then scores clipped text. Make the cut a plumbing-only exception and say how to avoid it.

Partial relay was treated as a finished pass: 36 of 87 named posts handed over for the entity, with no record of the remaining 51 in the handover step. The skill needs an explicit completeness rule before reporting.

Skill says ask only when blocked, yet the run stopped after the single query "jokowi" (99 of 100 opinions in 365d) and asked permission to continue. The Decided rule was ignored; make the completeness requirement explicit.
Observed timing on staging-run harvest: 30 steps in one JS call timed out; 8 steps per call returned in ~25s each. Step count in the skill was 10, which is the untested value.

Relaying all 275 captured posts was too much output. The JS pre-filter (target regex, other-tokoh denylist, length floor) cut them to 88 relayable rows, fitting the tool output limit and dropping multi-tokoh posts before they reach staging.

Data minimization: opinion rows were written to scratch files during the run. The skill never said where scratch lives or when to delete it; state it so rows do not linger in the repo or carry handles.

The episode's pre-check ran as a single env-gated script, dry run by default, which is safer than separate dry-run and submit steps. The yield (8 of 62 pass, most dropped as no_class) is needed to plan collection volume.

Reconcile with trace: the skill said the submit does not refresh aggregates, but the 365d snapshot recalculated within about a minute of the 8-row submit. The old statement is superseded by this evidence.
A verification query used sentiment_class, which does not exist, and failed. The real column is sentiment; recording the names saves a failed round trip to staging.

Second Jokowi run showed the in-browser lexicon filter lifted the staging pre-check pass rate from 8/66 to 36/36, so relay tokens were no longer spent on rows the classifier would reject with no_class. The skill only described target/denylist/length filtering.
Keeps the pre-check expectation consistent with the new in-page lexicon filter so a future run does not read a low pass rate as a pipeline problem.
